notes:
Lead profile: SMB, fast-growing helpdesk SaaS focused on small-mid ecom brands.
Primary contact: Samir Patel, Founder (technical). CTO is part-time; engineering team ~6.
Why Redwood: self-serve hosted API looks simplest for quick rollout; care about predictable per-token costs and avoiding noisy 429s for customers.

Current integration status:
- Using SDK prototype (JS) in staging. Calls to /v1/generate for chat + /v1/embeddings for KB similarity.
- Typical steady-state: 4-8 rps per customer. Peak pattern: daily 09:00-10:00 and big spikes when merchant import runs (~200 users triggering support flows).
- Observed behavior: when import-triggered spike hits ~60 concurrent requests we see 429s and retries amplify traffic.

Requirements & priorities (from call):
- Primary: avoid customer-visible 429s during expected automated spikes. Prefer graceful queuing or clear Retry-After headers.
- Soft reqs: cost sensitivity; want guidance on batching/aggregation to reduce token spend (some long merchant notes).
- Latency target: p95 < 700ms for chat short-turn responses; acceptable up to 2s for long summaries.
- Throughput: single-tenant hosted API for now; anticipate scale to Dedicated only if ARR > $50k/yr.
- Model preference: open/efficient models (quantized friendly) — lower token spend > bleeding-edge quality.

Suggested Redwood capabilities discussed:
- Quota tiers for dev vs prod, per-key burst allowance, auto-backoff / Retry-After propagation, and recommended concurrency limits per key.
- Prefix caching for repeated KB queries; advice on batch embeddings upload cadence.

Action items / notes from AE/SE:
- SE (Liam) to provide concrete concurrency guidance: requests/sec per key, recommended client-side queueing strategy, and example exponential backoff with jitter.
- AE (Maya) to schedule a hosted API burst test (100 concurrent short chat requests, 30s sustained) — need results by 2026-03-15.
- Customer asks for an explicit SMB quota escalation path and a visible dashboard metric for "quota headroom".

Quotes / call snippets:
- Samir: "We can tolerate slower responses for summaries, but 429s during merchant imports are killing user experience."
- Samir: "If we can throttle gracefully and show customers a queue, we can stay on hosted for awhile."

Risks / concerns:
- Retry storms from client-side naive retry on 429. Need guidance and sample client libs.
- No SLA on free tier — customer worried about production risk if they scale quickly.

Docs/shared artifacts: pricing deck + burst test plan linked. SE asked for sample code to implement token-aware batching.
